intro: A curated starting point for trainers. Every link goes to the organization's own site. Material from other organizations is linked, not copied. Suggest an addition through the Subscribe page.

categories.title: Sowards Consulting free reference cards
categories.description: Printable one-page references built from the Sowards frameworks. The two below are available inside this app.

links.title: PC 835a After AB 392
links.description: What the law actually requires of California officers, the four framing errors, and the post-AB 392 documentation checklist.

links.title: Downing the Duck
links.description: The six-stage staff manipulation framework for juvenile facilities, with warning signs and supervisor duties.

categories.title: Find and read the opinions
categories.description: Primary sources. Read the opinion itself before relying on a summary, including the ones in this app.

links.title: CourtListener
links.description: Free full-text search of federal and state opinions from the Free Law Project, with docket alerts.

links.title: Supreme Court of the United States
links.description: Slip opinions, order lists, and dockets.

links.title: Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals
links.description: Published opinions and unpublished memoranda for California, Oregon, Washington, Arizona, Nevada, and the rest of the circuit.

links.title: California Courts: Opinions
links.description: California Supreme Court and Court of Appeal opinions, published and unpublished.

links.title: Legal Information Institute (Cornell)
links.description: Free U.S. Code, Constitution, Supreme Court opinions, and plain-language explanations.

links.title: Justia
links.description: Free case law, codes, and regulations.

categories.title: Other legal update publishers
categories.description: National case law digests worth reading alongside the weekly brief. Most are written for policing; the weekly brief here adds the custody, probation, and juvenile layer and ends every case with how to train it.

links.title: Xiphos (Lexipol)
links.description: Ken Wallentine's monthly criminal procedure and use of force newsletter. Free for public safety officers, educators, and public attorneys.

links.title: LLRMI Legal Updates
links.description: Jack Ryan's frequent case summaries on search, seizure, use of force, and jail liability, with Supreme Court roundups.

links.title: Daigle Law Group Legal Updates
links.description: Case law posts, on-demand courses, and an annual Use of Force Summit.

links.title: CPOA Legislative and Legal Digest
links.description: The California Peace Officers' Association annual digest of new California laws, prepared with the Attorney General's office and the CHP.

categories.title: California statutes and standards
categories.description: The California layer that sits on top of federal law. Train to this standard, not to the most forgiving federal circuit.

links.title: Penal Code section 835a
links.description: Use of force by peace officers, as amended by AB 392.

links.title: Government Code section 7286
links.description: Required agency use-of-force policy contents, including the feasibility language.

links.title: California Legislative Information
links.description: Search every California code section and bill, including Penal Code 69, 148, 417.3, and Welfare and Institutions Code provisions.

links.title: Commission on POST
links.description: Peace Officer Standards and Training: regulations, learning domains, and certified course catalog.

links.title: Board of State and Community Corrections (BSCC)
links.description: Standards and Training for Corrections (STC), Title 15 regulations, and facility inspection standards.

categories.title: Liability, research, and policy organizations
categories.description: National organizations that publish case digests, research, and model policy. Some are membership or subscription based.

links.title: Police1 videos and Use of Force section
links.description: News, legal analysis, and video series including Reality Training and Bodycam Briefings that walk through real encounters. Free with registration; Lexipol owns the site.

links.title: Police1 original videos
links.description: The video library: Reality Training with Dave Smith, body camera breakdowns, and tactical debriefs for roll call and classroom use. Link to them; do not download or re-host.

links.title: Corrections1
links.description: The corrections side of the same network: custody news, legal columns, and training articles for jails, prisons, and juvenile facilities.

links.title: AELE (Americans for Effective Law Enforcement)
links.description: Legal publications, case summaries, and seminars for police, corrections, and public employment law.

links.title: Force Science Institute
links.description: Human factors research on reaction time, perception, memory under stress, and force encounters.

links.title: Police Executive Research Forum (PERF)
links.description: Integrating Communications, Assessment, and Tactics (ICAT) and the Critical Decision-Making Model.

links.title: International Association of Chiefs of Police (IACP)
links.description: Model policies, training keys, and the National Consensus Policy on Use of Force.

links.title: National Institute of Justice
links.description: Federal research on use of force, less-lethal technology, and officer safety.

links.title: National Institute of Corrections
links.description: Free corrections training, technical assistance, and a research library.

links.title: PREA Resource Center
links.description: PREA standards, audit instruments, and training for adult and juvenile facilities.

links.title: Lexipol
links.description: Policy, training, and the Police1 and Corrections1 news sites.

categories.title: California use-of-force instructors and training centers
categories.description: California instructors and training centers that teach use of force law and tactics. Listings are chosen by Sowards Consulting. Some are also competitors for training budgets; they are listed because trainers will look for them anyway.

links.title: Savage Training Group
links.description: POST-certified use of force decision-making and legal update workshops, supervisor courses, and an online PC 835a course. Based in California.

links.title: CSU Long Beach Center for Criminal Justice Research and Training
links.description: The 24-hour Use of Force Train the Trainer course that meets the POST instructor requirement in CCR section 1070.

links.title: Chief Probation Officers of California (CPOC) STC courses
links.description: Short STC-certified online courses for probation staff, including new laws updates and felony sentencing.
